content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 25. Supplemental: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 viewpoint concepts. This unit focuses on security as a cross-cutting perspective.

A perspective applies cross-cutting analysis across several views. The security perspective examines how architecture decisions affect confidentiality, integrity, availability, accountability, authorization, authentication, and threat exposure.
Security cannot be added only at the end. It shapes context boundaries, data ownership, deployment zones, operational controls, dependency management, and incident response.
Studio: annotate a context diagram with trust boundaries, sensitive data flows, identities, and external attack surfaces.

concepts.name: Architecture perspective
concepts.description: A cross-cutting set of activities and checks applied across views to address a quality concern.

concepts.name: Security perspective
concepts.description: A perspective focused on protecting assets, reducing threats, and preserving security properties across the architecture.

concepts.name: Security property
concepts.description: A desired protection quality such as confidentiality, integrity, availability, accountability, or non-repudiation.

concepts.name: Attack surface
concepts.description: The set of entry points and exposed interactions through which an attacker might affect the system.
